Name: Rationalism
Description: The view that reason and a priori argument, rather than sense experience, are the primary route to certain knowledge.

Name: Logical / Analytic Method
Description: Knowledge pursued through formal logic, precise conceptual analysis, and careful attention to language and argument structure.

Name: Faith / Scripture / Contemplative Insight
Description: Knowledge grounded in religious faith, scripture, revelation, or direct contemplative or meditative insight.

Name: Empiricism
Description: The view that knowledge derives primarily from sense experience and observation rather than innate ideas.

Name: Critical / Social Theory Method
Description: Knowledge pursued through critical analysis of ideology, power, and social structure, often with an emancipatory aim.

Name: Hermeneutics / Textual Interpretation
Description: Knowledge pursued through careful interpretation of texts, traditions, and their historical and cultural context.

Name: Pragmatism
Description: The view that beliefs are justified by their practical workability and consequences rather than correspondence to fixed truth.

Name: Skepticism
Description: Systematic doubt about the possibility of certain knowledge, used as a method of inquiry or a philosophical conclusion.

Name: Intuitionism
Description: The view that some truths, especially moral truths, are known directly through rational or moral intuition rather than argument.

Name: Genealogical / Deconstructive Method
Description: Knowledge pursued by tracing the historical origins of concepts or by unsettling the fixed oppositions within a text or tradition.

Name: Phenomenology
Description: Knowledge pursued through careful first-person description of conscious experience as it presents itself.

Name: Dialectical Method
Description: Knowledge pursued through the back-and-forth of question, contradiction, and synthesis between opposing positions.

Name: Foundationalism / Constructivism
Description: The view that justified belief rests on secure foundational premises, or alternatively is actively constructed through reasoned agreement.

Name: Thought Experiments
Description: Knowledge pursued through imagined scenarios designed to test and clarify our concepts and intuitions.

Name: Scientific Method
Description: Knowledge pursued through empirical observation, hypothesis, and experimental testing modeled on the natural sciences.
